review_notes: Read all 426 lines of the target and inspected the relevant definitions and divergence-free API in FourierLeray.lean and FourierRealification.lean. I found the substantive repeated proof machinery in the Leray and Stokes representative theorems: both unfold a Fourier multiplier operator, transfer the transform equality to an a.e. equality, and combine it with the corresponding divergence-free multiplier lemma. I did not report the similar five-line realification wrappers at 384-390 and 417-424 separately because they are thin applications of `realPartVectorL2Representative_eq_ae` and `isWeakDivFree_congr_ae`, below the rubric's nontriviality threshold. Exact elaboration of the proposed helper was not tested; its typeclass arguments may need routine adjustment.

findings.problem: The two proofs at 368-380 and 399-413 perform the same frequency-to-physical transfer. In each case the proof unfolds the physical operator as `ℱV.symm (M (ℱX v))`, proves its `ℱV`-transform is `M (ℱX v)` by `apply_symm_apply`, turns that equality into an a.e. equality with `Lp.ext_iff`, and feeds the already-proved divergence-free range of the multiplier to `realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal`. The Leray and Stokes cases differ only by `X = ComplexVec3` versus `ComplexTensor3` and by the multiplier. This repeated bridge is the main content of both proofs, not just notation, and another multiplier will have to copy the same four steps again.
findings.proposed_change:
Introduce one helper immediately before these theorems, using only the already imported Lp/Fourier API:

```lean
private theorem realPartVectorL2Representative_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierSymmMultiplier
    {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℂ X] [CompleteSpace X]
    (T : Lp (α := L2Vec3) X 2 → ComplexVectorL2)
    (M : Lp (α := L2Vec3) X 2 → ComplexVectorL2)
    (v : Lp (α := L2Vec3) X 2)
    (hT : T v =
      (MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 ComplexVec3).symm
        (M ((MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 X) v)))
    (hM : ∀ᵐ ξ ∂volume,
      inner ℂ (complexifyFrequency ξ)
        (M ((MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 X) v) ξ) = 0) :
    CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 (realPartVectorL2Representative (T v)) := by
  have hFourier : ∀ᵐ ξ ∂volume,
      inner ℂ (complexifyFrequency ξ)
        ((MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 ComplexVec3) (T v) ξ) = 0 := by
    let ℱV := MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 ComplexVec3
    let ℱX := MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 X
    have h : ℱV (ℱV.symm (M (ℱX v))) = M (ℱX v) := ℱV.apply_symm_apply _
    rw [hT]
    filter_upwards [(Lp.ext_iff).mp h, hM] with ξ hξ hMξ
    rw [hξ]
    exact hMξ
  exact realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal (T v) hFourier
```

The Leray proof then becomes `exact realPartVectorL2Representative_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierSymmMultiplier (T := lerayProjectionL2) (M := lerayFourierMultiplier) (v := complexifyVectorL2 f) (by rfl) (lerayFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae _)`, and the Stokes proof becomes the same call with `T := stokesL2Operator ht`, `M := stokesFourierMultiplier ht`, `v := complexifyTensorL2 F`, and `stokesFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae ht _`. The existing hypotheses are preserved: Leray remains unconditional in `f`, while Stokes keeps `ht : 0 < t` and `F : RealTensorL2`; the `t = 0` case is still excluded exactly as before.
findings.benefit: The common Fourier-transform and a.e.-orthogonality argument is proved once, so the two public theorems state only their multiplier-specific data. A reader can see immediately that the only differences are the domain `ComplexVec3` or `ComplexTensor3` and the chosen Fourier multiplier. Future multiplier cases can reuse the same theorem, and the explicit `hT` and `hM` parameters make the required transform identity and frequency-orthogonality hypothesis visible and harder to mix up.
